description: ocsp.rs lines 17-19: der_failed() returns der::Error::new(ErrorKind::Failed, Length::ZERO). This is used in two places: when response_bytes is None after a Successful status, and when responseType \!= id-pkix-ocsp-basic. Both cases surface as Error::OcspParseError(e) where e carries no information about what went wrong. A caller inspecting the error chain cannot distinguish 'missing responseBytes' from 'wrong responseType' from a genuine DER parse failure. This makes debugging and logging difficult. Introduce a dedicated error variant or at minimum use distinct ErrorKind values.
title: der_failed() returns opaque error with no diagnostic information
